newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyushu Electric chooses electricity wholesalers.
newsitem.headline: Kyushu Electric chooses electricity wholesalers.

text.p: Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc said on Thursday that it had selected Nippon Steel Corp and Kyushu Oil Co Ltd as its long-term electricity providers, as a result of a tender.

Each firm will provide Kyushu Electric, which serves seven prefectures in the southwestern Japanese island of Kyushu, with 137,000 kilowatts (kw) of electricity for about 15 years starting in 1999, a spokesman for the electric utility said.
Kyushu Oil will build a 149,000 kw power plant, which will run on residual oil, at its 136,000 barrel-per-day Oita refinery, a spokesman for the oil firm said.
Building the power station is estimated to cost 25 billion yen, he added.
Nippon Steel plans to set up a 149,000 kw coal-fired power station at its Yawata plant in Fukuoka prefecture in Kyushu, a spokesman for the major steelmaker said.
